♻ ☆ CardioLoom: A Report-Guided Electrocardiogram Foundation Model for Cross-Domain Cardiovascular Phenotyping
Ziqing Yu, Yuhui Tao, Jiayu Huo, Lei Pan, Zilong Xiao, Juecheng Chen, Xiao Li, Jianxuan Li, You Zhou, Zhixing Li, Cong Wang, Beijian Zhang, Chen Chen, Hongyang Lu, Konstantinos Patlatzoglou, Daniel B. Kramer, Jonathan W. Waks, Yangang Su, Fu Siong Ng, Shuo Wang, Yixiu Liang, Junbo Ge
Routine electrocardiogram (ECG) reports offer scalable supervision for cardiovascular representation learning. In this retrospective study, we pretrained CardioLoom, a report-guided ECG foundation model, on 2,781,289 ECG-report pairs from 1,298,359 patients. Downstream development used a separate cohort of 721,317 ECGs from 233,798 patients. Evaluation covered 89 targets, with external testing in nine cohorts. Across 45 internal ECG diagnoses, macro area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.624 versus 0.615 for DeepECG-SSL. Across 203 external ECG evaluations, corresponding means were 0.425 and 0.424. Using labels from 10% of training patients, CardioLoom achieved macro-AUPRC 0.559, exceeding supervised training with all labels (0.549). For heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, AUPRCs were 0.690, 0.641 and 0.677 in Zhongshan, Shiyuan and BIDMC. Cardiac amyloidosis screening yielded 4.5% positive predictive value using a threshold targeting 99% specificity in validation. Report-guided pretraining supported label-efficient ECG diagnosis, with variable transfer across echocardiographic phenotypes.
comment: 135 pages, 5 main figures, 7 supplementary figures and 31 supplementary tables. Substantially revised; ECGCLIP renamed CardioLoom. Updated pretraining methods, cohort accounting, baseline comparisons, statistical analyses and supplementary materials
♻ ☆ On the use of case estimate and transactional payment data in neural networks for individual loss reserving
Benjamin Avanzi, Matthew Lambrianidis, Greg Taylor, Bernard Wong
The use of neural networks trained on individual claims data has become increasingly popular in the actuarial reserving literature. We consider how to best input historical payment data in neural network models. Additionally, case estimates are also available in the format of a time series, and we extend our analysis to assessing their predictive power. In this paper, we compare a feed-forward neural network trained on summarised transactions to a recurrent neural network equipped to analyse a claim's entire payment history and/or case estimate development history. We draw conclusions from training and comparing the performance of the models on multiple, comparable highly complex datasets simulated from SPLICE (Avanzi, Taylor and Wang, 2023). In environments where covariate data is limited, we find evidence that case estimates will improve predictions substantially, but that equipping the neural network with memory only leads to meagre improvements. Although the case estimation process and quality will vary significantly between insurers, we provide a standardised methodology for assessing their value.
♻ ☆ Memorization capacity of deep ReLU neural networks characterized by width and depth
Xin Yang, Yunfei Yang
This paper studies the memorization capacity of deep neural networks with ReLU activation. Specifically, we investigate the minimal size of such networks to memorize any $N$ data points in the unit ball with pairwise separation distance $δ$ and labels from a finite set of size $C$. Most prior studies characterize the memorization capacity by the number of parameters or neurons. We extend these results by constructing ReLU networks with adjustable width $W$ and depth $L$ satisfying $W^2L^2\log W=\mathcal{O}(N(\log(δ^{-1})+\log C))$ that can memorize any such dataset. We also establish width-depth lower bounds that depend explicitly on $δ$ and $C$ for networks capable of memorizing all such datasets. When $\log(δ^{-1})\asymp\log N$, our construction achieves $W^2L^2\asymp N$ for suitable choices of width and depth. This order is optimal if $\log C\asymp\log N$, and optimal up to logarithmic factors if $\log C=o(\log N)$.
♻ ☆ Sampling Design and Confidence Tubes for Integral Curves on Riemannian Manifolds
Xiaotian Chang, Qirui Hu, Cyrus Mostajeran
We estimate the integral curve of an unknown vector field from noisy tangent vector field on a known compact Riemannian manifold. We consider two sampling settings: independent observations at random locations that have already been collected, and a fixed response budget that allows subsequent locations to be chosen using pilot information. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the passive kernel estimator has curve error of order $n^{-2/(d+3)}$ in probability, with sample size $n$ and manifold dimension $d$. Its functional central limit theorem has a limit characterized by a linear stochastic differential equation. For active sampling, an independent pilot directs one new batch of measurements to neighborhoods of the target curve. Under localization, smoothness and design conditions, this concentration yields expected maximum curve error of order $N^{-1/2}$, including the pilot in the total response budget $N$. Both methods provide simultaneous geodesic confidence tubes with asymptotically exact coverage under mild conditions. Simulations show narrower active tubes in most reported settings, with improved small-sample coverage in some three-dimensional examples. Ocean-drifter observations illustrate mean-flow reconstruction on the sphere, and a canopy-flow LDA application uses retrospective active sampling to quantify lateral and vertical departures of local mean streamlines.
♻ ☆ Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension
Ernesto Araya, Gitta Kutyniok, Weilin Li, Johannes Maly, Manjot Singh
In this work, we formalize the concept of intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes introduced in Li et al. (2018), which measures the structural complexity of learning problems by training along randomly generated subspaces. We define the intrinsic dimension of a set $Θ\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ as the minimal dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(Θ)$ such that a random plane of dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(Θ)$ in $\mathbb{R}^p$ intersects $Θ$ with probability one. We show that it is a generalized notion of co-dimension that depends on the global geometry of $Θ$. We study mathematical properties of the intrinsic dimension and develop techniques to estimate the intrinsic dimension of sets $Θ$ that arise in learning problems. More specifically, we derive upper and/or lower bounds where $Θ$ is the set of optimal parameters in student-teacher settings with shallow and deep ReLU networks, including finite and infinite sample cases, and with and without regularization. We discuss how our theory leads to novel types of generalization bounds, thereby showing that the intrinsic dimension is a measure of learning complexity. Our results connect techniques from seemingly different areas of machine learning research such as classification of symmetries of ReLU networks and stochastic geometry.
♻ ☆ Neural Classifiers as Error-Correcting Codes
Sergey Salishev, Anton Makarov, Oleg Granichin, Renata Avros, Zeev Volkovich
A unified framework is proposed that characterizes supervised deep classification as the decoding of error-correcting codes in the Shannon sense. Cross-entropy optimization is shown to align softmax classifiers with maximum-likelihood decoding, where logits map to Hamming distances to class-specific codewords. This correspondence explains the emergence of standard divergence objectives (e.g., Kullback-Leibler, Jeffreys, Bregman) and provides a geometric basis for the stability of decision boundaries. Furthermore, the geometries of Neural Collapse and LeJEPA are identified as optimal constellations for decoding under isotropic noise. Unlike classical Error-Correcting Output Codes, deep networks are shown to learn effective codebooks in the feature space implicitly. This insight is leveraged to derive novel criteria for lossless quantization, improved knowledge distillation, and architectural regularization based on code redundancy. Finally, this perspective is extended to self-supervised encoders, offering a cohesive explanation for the geometry of latent representations in modern neural models.

♻ ☆ Evaluating and Mitigating Skin Color Bias in Skin Lesion Classificatio
Kuniko Paxton, Koorosh Aslansefat, Dhavalkumar Thakker, Yiannis Papadopoulos
Skin lesion classifiers may overlook performance disparity because of subtle skin tone variations by treating skin tone as a categorical attribute. This study proposes a method that represents skin tone as a continuous attribute and assigns individual weights to each sample based on its nonlinear relationship with classification performance. Evaluations on two dermatological datasets showed that fairness metrics were sensitive to skin-color categorization. The proposed method also demonstrated more stable fairness improvements than conventional categorical reweighting while generally preserving classification performance.
♻ ☆ Estimating aerosol particle number size distributions from PM2.5 with physics-regularized flow matching
Zhi-Song Liu, Jenni Köykkä, Wenqing Peng, Ammar Kheder, Petri Clusius, Michael Boy
The mass concentration of particles smaller than 2.5um (PM2.5) is cheap to measure and widely monitored, whereas the particle number size distribution (PNSD) requires costly instruments and is measured at only a few research stations. Yet many aerosol effects, such as vapor uptake, cloud droplet formation and deposition in the human respiratory tract, depend on the PNSD rather than on mass. We explore whether generative deep learning models can infer the current PNSD from routine data: from the PM2.5 record and eight meteorological variables over a 24h window, a model generates an ensemble of plausible hourly PNSDs for the same window, reflecting that one mass can arise from many size distributions. Rather than proposing a single best model, we use two contrasting Finnish stations, the boreal forest site Hyytiala and the urban site Kumpula, as a controlled testbed. On it, we benchmark six generative models against deterministic regression and historical-mean baselines, locally and after transfer between sites, and test physical constraints for neural network training. Flow matching performs best overall; its guided variant has the lowest continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) at both sites. A constraint based on a reduced aerosol general dynamic equation (GDE) lowers the CRPS by 5.5-11.5% at the training site and reduces errors after transfer between sites. Transfer remains harder than local estimation, identifying multi-station training as the next step towards PNSD estimates at unmonitored locations. This benchmark establishes physics-informed generative models as a promising route from routine air-quality monitoring to size-resolved aerosol information.

♻ ☆ Kernel-based guarantees for nonlinear parametric models in Bayesian optimization NeurIPS 2026
Rafael Oliveira
Modern Bayesian optimization and adaptive sampling methods increasingly rely on nonlinear parametric models, such as neural networks, yet theoretical guarantees for such models under adaptive data collection remain limited. Existing analyses largely focus on Gaussian processes, kernel machines, linear models, or linearized neural approximations, leaving a gap between theory and the nonlinear models used in practice. We develop a kernel-based framework for analyzing regularized parametric models trained on adaptively collected data. Our approach uses kernels over the parameter space to induce reproducing kernel Hilbert space structures over the corresponding model class, yielding confidence bounds for models trained with a broad class of regularized losses. We show how these bounds can establish convergence guarantees for approximate Thompson sampling and provide a foundation for analyzing broader likelihood-free Bayesian optimization methods. These results provide a unified route to analyzing nonlinear models in Bayesian optimization and related adaptive optimization settings.

☆ CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
Junyi Shen, Yao Lu
Coding agents make videos by writing and refining programs in a build--inspect--edit loop. A finished film costs a median of $2.85 in model calls and 11 minutes, over a third of that time in builds that block the agent. We find that much of this time is avoidable, for two reasons. First, 37.5% of the frames of a session's later films were drawn before, many shifted in time or inside an edited scene. Second, half of the builds stop at a check, where the agent needs only the verdict, but which builds stop is unknown until the checks finish. We present CodeReel, a training-free execution layer behind agents' existing commands. Exact frame reuse keys each frame by its drawing commands, regardless of its position in time, and reuses each frame whose key recurs. Blocking-aware scheduling runs the checks first and starts the render alongside them, at idle priority, unless the session's recent builds make a pass unlikely. Scheduling spends CPU to answer sooner and reuse returns it; exact keys let later versions use frames rendered for a failed one as the agent thinks. We introduce EditLoop, a benchmark of replayable agent sessions whose films are checked against renders from scratch. On it, CodeReel cuts the agent's wait by 36.3% against Rebuild, a warm pipeline with parallel rendering, and by 57.9% against Sequential, today's step-by-step pipeline. On time-shifting edits its reuse renders 43.9%, close to the 43.0% whose pixels are new, while Manim-style caching renders 99.8%. With real agents, the median wait per build is 0.62x Rebuild's in Claude Code, on topics never used in development, and 0.67x in Codex CLI. The gain holds for five models and two frameworks.

☆ LeViT-UNet++: Towards Balanced Fine-Grained Details and Context for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
Guoping Xu, Jinling Zhu, Liuyue Li
Efficient medical image segmentation is essential for clinical applications requiring fast and accurate delineation, such as surgical navigation, radiation therapy, and real-time image-guided intervention. Despite substantial advances in convolutional neural networks and Transformers, attaining high accuracy under limited computational resources remains difficult, because reducing model complexity often sacrifices fine-grained structural details and global context modeling, yielding an unfavorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. To address this, we propose LeViT-UNet++, an efficient encoder-decoder architecture that better balances local detail preservation and global context modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Haar Wavelet Multi-Scale Downsampling (HWMD) module that decomposes feature representations into low- and high-frequency components to extract multi-scale structural information, thereby mitigating detail loss during downsampling. We further develop a depthwise convolution-based decoder that integrates multi-scale global representations from Transformer blocks with local spatial features, enabling progressive feature refinement while reducing computational overhead. Evaluated on four benchmarks (Synapse, ACDC, LA2018, and MSD Heart) under both 2D and 3D settings, LeViT-UNet++ achieves competitive accuracy with a compact parameter footprint and fast inference. On Synapse, for instance, it attains a DSC of 76.57% with only 8.025M parameters and 241.72 FPS, confirming a favorable accuracy-efficiency balance. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining wavelet-based multi-scale feature extraction with lightweight local-global feature fusion for efficient medical segmentation. The source code is available at https://github.com/apple1986/levit_unet_pp.

☆ Streaming Generative Video Compression with Embedding Alignment and In-Context Propagation
Zhitao Wang, Hengyu Man, Han Liu, Wenrui Li, Debin Zhao, Xiaopeng Fan
Video compression at ultra-low bitrates presents substantial challenges in preserving perceptual quality. Although pretrained video diffusion transformers (DiTs) provide powerful generative priors, existing generative video compression (GVC) methods built on them typically rely on computationally expensive VAE decoders to reconstruct video frames. Moreover, jointly refining multiple frames to exploit the inherent spatiotemporal modeling capabilities of video DiTs introduces additional buffering delay. To address these challenges, we propose SGVC, a streaming generative video compression framework that adapts a pretrained latent video DiT into a causal pixel-space refiner. Specifically, SGVC projects decoded features from a contextual pixel codec directly into the DiT input embedding space. To bridge the representation gap between codec-derived embeddings and pretrained DiT embeddings, we introduce Embedding Alignment, which aligns the projected embeddings with input embeddings extracted from the original frames during training. The refined DiT hidden states are then mapped directly to the pixel domain through a lightweight reconstruction path, bypassing the pretrained VAE decoder. To further exploit the spatiotemporal priors of the video DiT while maintaining causal decoding, we introduce In-Context Propagation, which reuses layer-wise K/V states across frames to exploit historical generative context, improving temporal consistency without requiring clip-wise buffering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SGVC achieves competitive rate-perception performance, with average BD-rate savings of 71.97% over S$^2$VC in terms of DISTS. Project Page: https://chigland.github.io/SGVC/
comment: 15 pages, 18 figures, 5 tables, including supplementary material
♻ ☆ Words Speak Louder? Exploring the Language Shortcut of LLM-Driven Incomplete Multimodal Learning
Qiangchang Wang, Chong Xiao, Xiaokun Bai, Rundong He, Zhuang Qi, Xusheng Liang, Zhibin Wu, Wenhao Li
Is a face or a voice still heard once the words are known? Incomplete multimodal learning increasingly uses large language models (LLMs) as fusion engines: modality features enter as token blocks and missing modalities become placeholders. We find that LLM-driven fusion can override non-verbal evidence it can read. Contrasting its full-input prediction with counterfactual views, the same model shown one modality or no content, we identify language shortcuts. We build MR-Bench: MR-Bench-A types every test sample of four sentiment benchmarks; MR-Bench-H contains 900 human-validated clips (620 language-shortcut, LS; 280 non-verbal-shortcut, NS) from seven sources, and every model is scored on all of them. Zero-shot MLLMs solve at most 32.7% of the LS clips; adding the transcript to the muted video lowers vision-language accuracy by 46.1-53.1 points. Yet inverting a text-only model's answers solves 94.4%, so LS accuracy alone cannot establish use of non-verbal evidence. Inside the fusion LLM, fused states align increasingly with the text view late in the decoder. Counterfactual-View Reliability learning (CoVeR) trains views as unimodal judges and withholds fused supervision where they disagree. It achieves state-of-the-art results on five benchmarks without extra inference cost in accuracy mode. On MR-Bench-H, it reaches 61.7% LS and 93.6% NS accuracy; robust mode raises LS accuracy to 63.0% while lowering NS accuracy to 84.8%. Among LS clips solved without text, adding text causes errors on 30.1% with CoVeR versus 32.2% with LLM-Fusion. Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/CoVeR/.
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 14 tables. Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/CoVeR/
♻ ☆ DAT: Dual-Aware Adaptive Transmission with Small-Large Model Collaboration for Edge-Cloud Anomaly Detection AAAI 2027
Qi Guo, Zheming Yang, Yunqing Hu, Chang Zhao, Wen Ji
Continuous video anomaly detection is critical for timely safety monitoring in edge--cloud visual systems, but it remains challenging because abnormal events are sparse, transient, and require both low-latency anomaly detection and verifiable visual evidence. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer strong semantic understanding and visual reasoning capabilities for such event-centric analysis, yet applying them to continuous video streams incurs prohibitive computation and communication overhead under bandwidth-constrained edge--cloud deployments. To address this challenge, we propose DAT, a dual-aware adaptive transmission framework that supports high-quality semantic generation, low-latency anomaly detection, and progressive visual evidence supplementation. DAT first uses a collaborative small--large model cascade, where a lightweight edge-side model filters non-target-event frames, performs object detection, and triggers MLLM inference only for suspicious frames. Building on this cascade, DAT introduces visual guidance and semantic prompting to improve structured event understanding, localization, and output consistency. It further schedules semantic anomaly alarms and visual evidence through a semantic- and bandwidth-aware multi-stream transmission optimization method. Experimental results show that DAT achieves 97.77\% F1 in traffic-accident detection while substantially reducing inference and communication overhead. On continuous video workloads, DAT lowers the MLLM call rate to 13.71\% and reduces upload volume by at least 95.72\% compared with representative edge--cloud baselines. Under severe congestion, DAT reduces weighted alarm delay by up to 87.9\%, demonstrating efficient MLLM-based anomaly detection under constrained edge--cloud networks.
comment: 9 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to AAAI 2027
♻ ☆ AutoMV: An Automatic Multi-Agent System for Music Video Generation
Xiaoxuan Tang, Xinping Lei, Chaoran Zhu, Shiyun Chen, Ruibin Yuan, Yizhi Li, Changjae Oh, Ge Zhang, Wenhao Huang, Emmanouil Benetos, Yang Liu, Jiaheng Liu, Yinghao Ma
Turning a full song into a music video (MV) requires interpreting its lyrics, which are often metaphorical, multilingual, and repeated across choruses, together with its musical character, and laying the resulting imagery out along the song's structure. Existing music-to-video systems produce short clips or audio-reactive visuals and make little use of lyric meaning. We present AutoMV, a training-free multi-agent framework in which LLM Screenwriter and Director agents plan a full-song visual narrative from time-aligned lyrics and music analysis, keep characters consistent through a shared character bank, and route each shot to cinematic or lip-sync rendering with verification. To evaluate full-song MVs, we build M2VBench: 30 released songs paired with their official MVs, objective audio--visual metrics, and a 12-criterion rubric rated by music-industry experts. Expert evaluation shows that AutoMV outperforms other baselines, although a gap remains to human-produced MVs. Ablation studies highlight the importance of time-aligned lyrics for musical theme alignment and storytelling. We further find that the selected multimodal judge, guided by our evaluation rubric, recovers the expert ranking of automatic systems, with some discrepancies in fine-grained assessments.
♻ ☆ Relation-Aware Evidence Routing and Confidence-Guided Adaptation for Zero-Shot Visual Anomaly Detection
Xinyu Zhao, Yang Hu, Jiayi Luo, Qingyun Sun, Jianxin Li
Zero-shot visual anomaly detection (ZSAD) aims to identify and localize anomalies in unseen categories without target-domain adaptation, yet heterogeneous anomaly patterns and cross-domain variations challenge reliable detection. Existing approaches primarily rely on local visual features, patch-text similarities, or memory-based retrieval, leaving inter-patch relational information underexplored in anomaly evidence modeling. In this paper, we propose RACE-AD, a relation-aware evidence routing and confidence-guided adaptation framework that integrates local anomaly responses with attention-derived relational information for generalizable ZSAD. To capture inter-patch relationships, we characterize the dispersion of visual attention distributions using Shannon entropy, providing complementary relational statistics beyond local anomaly evidence. To organize heterogeneous evidence, we introduce relation-aware routing that combines memory-derived normal/anomaly responses with attention entropy to construct image-conditioned representations through entropy-regularized soft aggregation. To mitigate unreliable retrieval responses under domain shift, we design confidence-guided adaptation that regulates anomaly-conditioned representations according to the strength of the memory anomaly evidence and the relational dispersion before visual-semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on ten industrial and medical benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of RACE-AD, achieving average image-level AUROC and AP scores of 91.9% and 93.7%, and pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO scores of 93.6% and 80.0%, respectively. Ablation and diagnostic analyses show that entropy-guided routing mainly improves region-level localization and that the confidence gate is essential under domain shift.
♻ ☆ Human-Data Interaction, Exploration, and Visualization Systems in the AI Era: Challenges and Opportunities
Jean-Daniel Fekete, Yifan Hu, Dominik Moritz, Arnab Nandi, Senjuti Basu Roy, Eugene Wu, Nikos Bikakis, George Papastefanatos, Panos K. Chrysanthis, Guoliang Li, Lingyun Yu
The rapid advancement of AI is transforming human-centered systems, with profound implications for human-AI interaction, human-data interaction, and visual analytics. In the AI era, data analysis increasingly involves large-scale, heterogeneous, and multimodal data that is predominantly unstructured, as well as foundation models such as LLMs and VLMs, which introduce additional uncertainty into analytical processes. These shifts expose persistent challenges for human-data interactive systems, including perceptually misaligned latency, scalability constraints, limitations of existing interaction and exploration paradigms, and growing uncertainty regarding the reliability and interpretability of AI-generated insights. Responding to these challenges requires moving beyond conventional efficiency and scalability metrics, redefining the roles of humans and machines in analytical workflows, and incorporating cognitive, perceptual, and design principles into every level of the human-data interaction stack. This paper investigates the challenges introduced by recent advances in AI and examines how these developments are reshaping the ways users engage with data, while outlining limitations and open research directions for building human-centered AI systems for interactive data analysis in the AI era.
